what_it_is: The raw object QoreX returned from native.signArbitrary for the LOANSHARK test message. Not edited, not regenerated, not retyped from a summary: the base64 values are copied verbatim from what was supplied.
sha256_of: The stored bytes of qorex-signarbitrary.json, exactly as committed.
sha256_of_parsed_note: SHA-256 over JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(file)). Recorded so a reader can confirm the content independently of whitespace and line endings.
provenance: Supplied through the chat session on 2026-11-16, not captured by a tool. There is therefore no HTTP status, Content-Type, block height or response byte count to record, and no transaction hash exists: signArbitrary signs but does not broadcast.
formatting_note: The stored file uses LF line endings and a trailing newline. The chat paste carried CRLF. Line endings are the only difference; every character of every base64 value is unchanged, which the parsed-content hash above lets another party check. .gitattributes marks fixtures/** as -text so a checkout on any platform keeps these bytes, and sha256 above stays reproducible.
integrity_checks_run: classical.publicKey and classical.signature and pq.signature are canonical base64 (regex, length divisible by 4, re-encode equals input).
classical.publicKey decodes to 33 bytes and classical.signature to 64 bytes.
pq.signature decodes to 4627 bytes, the ML-DSA-87 signature size.
classical.publicKey equals the on-chain ecdsa_pubkey of qor1385wkhky3qkjwq47t8904xrd6s82lmkfjnxxsr in fixtures/onchain-account-qor1385.json, so the response belongs to that account.
pq.signature does not contain the on-chain 2592-byte ML-DSA public key, which is consistent with source-lock claim 7: the pq object carries no public key.
contains_key_material: Public keys and signatures only. The classical public key is already published on chain. No private key, seed phrase or recovery code is present.
